claims.text: In FeNiCrCoCu coatings, high-temperature wear resistance is governed by formation of a protective oxide glaze layer.
In FeNiCrCoCu coatings, microscopic deformation during high-temperature sliding is governed by formation of a protective oxide glaze layer.
The alloy matrix's intrinsic structural sensitivity to tribochemical reactions determines whether a glaze layer forms sufficiently rapidly during sliding.
Introducing oxidation-prone alloying elements into FeNiCrCoCu will promote protective glaze-layer formation.
Tribo-oxidation produces a protective oxide glaze layer on the worn surface.
Dynamic strain aging contributes to the proposed high-temperature wear and deformation response.
Relative to the baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating, adding oxidation-prone alloying elements will improve wear resistance.
Relative to the baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating, adding oxidation-prone alloying elements will reduce microscopic deformation.
The predicted effects should hold over 600-800 °C.
A lack of improved wear resistance and reduced microscopic deformation after adding oxidation-prone elements would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify temperatures above 600 °C, whereas the stated boundary includes 600 °C.
The intervention proposes one compositional change, but the experiment varies both alloy composition and microstructure, so it does not isolate the stated intervention.
